label: Simple 4-Prompt Experimental

prompt_stages.pass_1_creative_story: Using the SOURCE MATERIAL and TONE GUARDRAILS provided in the run context below, write one complete radio-drama story. Hard limits: at most 8 scenes, 2-4 speaking characters, 250 words per scene. Prose only - do not output JSON in this pass.
prompt_stages.pass_2_creative_ledger_fill: Convert the story from the previous pass into the production story ledger. Emit ONLY valid JSON matching the LEDGER SCHEMA provided in the run context - use exactly its field names; do not invent fields. Include cast, lines, beats, source metadata, coda/source note, and visual directives.
prompt_stages.pass_3_technical_schema_cleanup: Repair the JSON from the previous pass so it satisfies the LEDGER SCHEMA in the run context exactly: required fields present, enum values legal, ids consistent, no extra fields. Emit ONLY the repaired JSON.
prompt_stages.pass_4_technical_ledger_audit: Audit the JSON from the previous pass: cast vs line speakers, character ids, beat ids, line ids, continuity, source note, visual directives. Emit ONLY the corrected JSON, or the single line AUDIT_FAILED: <reason> if it cannot be made valid.

job_prompts.story_seed: Read the source material given in this run and build one story seed from it alone. Name the people, the place, and the pressure the source itself supplies. Nothing later in this run invents story for you, so make the seed complete enough to build on. Write planning notes only: no dialogue and no scenes. Name the episode from a concrete detail in the source material.
job_prompts.story_arc: Turn the accepted seed into one arc that has a beginning, a turn, and an end. Give each act its own premise, and make each act change something the next act has to answer. Give speaking parts to the people the source needs. Write planning notes only; the announcer and the music sit outside these acts.
job_prompts.act_spine: Plan this act and no other. State its spine in plain words, the state it starts in, and the state it ends in. The exit state must differ from the entry state, and it must follow from what the people in this act do, not from a new event dropped in. Write planning notes only; no dialogue.
job_prompts.act_beats: Break this act's spine into ordered beats. Each beat is one intent: name who pushes, what that person wants, and what has changed when the beat ends. Keep the beats in the order they will play, and let them carry the act from its entry state to its exit state. Write beat intents only; do not write lines.
job_prompts.act_dialogue: Fill each assigned beat with words the characters say out loud. Give every row only its own speaker's spoken words: no stage directions, no narration, no delivery notes. Where the source gives a character words, carry them as the source wrote them, however blunt or violent, and keep that character's own diction. Use only the beats and characters you were given, in the order listed.
job_prompts.act_cleanup: Make every row speakable and change nothing else. Each row must hold either words a character says out loud or a music cue. Turn a stage direction into words that row's character says, or into a music cue; drop it only when it can be neither. Leave a row that is already spoken words exactly as it is, including words carried from the source.
job_prompts.announcer_open: Write only what the announcer says out loud to open the show. Say the title, the setting, the scene time, and each character name exactly as given, letter for letter; do not paraphrase or trade any of them for another word. Introduce the story and its people in one spoken passage. Write no stage directions and no music cues.
job_prompts.announcer_news_coda: Write only what the announcer says out loud to close the show. Turn from the story to the real source it came from, then say the given closing fact claim in full, word for word, exactly as handed to you. Return the closing fact id as fact_id. Never read a URL, a file name, or license text aloud.

examples: A stronger model writes a rich story first, then fills and repairs the ledger in technical passes.
tone_guardrails: Python should validate and repair structure, not secretly co-write the story.
No fallback to legacy_many_pass if this experiment fails.
Adaptive cleanup may continue only under a hard max pass cap and deterministic validator failures.
source_requirements: Any selected source bank must provide a valid source packet and story pack.
ledger_validation_notes: Pass 4 must check cast vs line speakers, character ids, beat ids, line ids, source metadata, coda/source note, and visual directives.
Optional adaptive cleanup stops when deterministic validators pass or max_cleanup_passes is reached.
